newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: 35 hurt in Australia New Year party accident.
newsitem.headline: 35 hurt in Australia New Year party accident.

text.p: A wooden balcony at a New Year's Eve party in the Australian city of Perth collapsed, injuring 35 people, 13 of them seriously, police said on Wednesday.

About 40 people aged 18 to 25 plunged five metres (15 feet) to the ground when the second-floor balcony of an apartment gave way, leaving many with head and spinal injuries, broken bones and lacerations, police said.
Party guest Zoe Williams, who was in the apartment at the time, said the party was not boisterous when the accident occurred half an hour before midnight in Western Australia.
"It was very civil at that point because it was still quite early in the evening," Williams told reporters.
"In fact people were still just having their first drinks, waiting for things to happen," she said.
Police spokesman Sergeant Steve Verkerk said it was not known if the weight of 40 people caused the collapse. "At this stage it's too early to speculate what might have caused the accident," he said.
New Year's Eve revellers around Australia were relatively subdued this year and police in several states said crowd numbers and arrests were down on last year's figures.
In Sydney, an estimated 400,000 people packed into the city and thousands more lined the harbour to watch a spectacular A$1 million (US$800,000) pyrotechnics display using more than 16,000 fireworks.
At Bondi, where rioting marred 1995 Christmas celebrations, about 8,000 people watched a 15-metre (45-foot) effigy of Old Man Time burned on the beach at midnight.
